title: Response timing archaeology: cohort-level quantile decomposition
content:
Purpose:
Quick investigation notes tracing a set of long-tail responses observed on 2024-11-06 across multiple models. This doc is an "archaeology" style timeline: raw observations -> reproduction steps -> per-stage quantile decomposition -> working hypotheses -> suggested next steps. Aim is a compact, shareable artifact for on-call + perf team sync.

Context / why I started:
- First alert: ops page spike in 99th percentile latency for the hosted text-generation route (model: rw-13b-fp16) on 2024-11-06 16:12 UTC.
- Scope: p50/p95/p99 increase limited to a small fraction of requests (~0.3% of traffic) but severe (p99 from ~280ms -> ~1.9s).
- Initial suspicion: intermittent KV-cache misses + unusual batching behavior when requests had long system prompts.

Data sources used:
- Sampled traces pulled from trace-storage between 2024-11-06T15:00 and 2024-11-06T18:00 (n = 9.3k traces, sampling ratio ~1:30).
- Telemetry: per-token timing histogram, batch wait times, kernel selection logs, socket egress counters.
- Replay harness: local trace-replay with prod-like config (same model binary, same quantization profile).

Summary numbers (overall):
- baseline (all traffic prior week): p50 210ms, p95 360ms, p99 520ms
- incident window (peak): p50 230ms, p95 420ms, p99 1,900ms
- incident cohort (subset with long prompts / system metadata): p50 310ms, p95 780ms, p99 1,870ms

Cohorting approach:
- short: prompt tokens <= 128
- mid: 129-512
- long: >512
- metadata-heavy: presence of heavy system directives, >8 tool-calls in prompt header

Per-stage decomposition (median of cohort, numbers in ms):
Stages: tokenization -> encoder-prep -> KV-read -> attention-step (per-token avg across seq) -> kernel-emit -> network-egress
- short cohort (p50): 8 -> 40 -> 6 -> 125 -> 18 -> 13 = ~210ms
- mid cohort (p50): 9 -> 48 -> 9 -> 210 -> 25 -> 19 = ~320ms
- long cohort (p50): 12 -> 62 -> 18 -> 400 -> 28 -> 30 = ~550ms

Tail (p99) breakdown for long cohort (representative sample medians):
- tokenization: 14ms (IQR 10-22)
- encoder-prep (includes normalization + input slicing): 95ms (IQR 60-220)
- KV-read (cold partial hits): 140ms (IQR 30-860) -- this is the largest variable contributor
- attention / decode loops: 1200ms (IQR 900-1,600) -- correlated with large batch micro-pauses
- kernel-emit: 160ms (IQR 90-320)
- network-egress: 150ms (IQR 110-240)

Observations and signals:
1) KV cache interaction:
   - A subset (~12%) of extreme p99 traces show a KV-read pattern where the cache lookup falls back to a slower path (disk-backed cold miss + async fill). These traces have a clear KV-read spike in the timeline and align with a recent rollout of a new cache eviction policy (PR referenced above).
   - Replay with cache warmed removed the ~140ms median spike, but attention/decode still dominated.

2) Batching anomalies / microburst stalls:
   - High attention/decode times in the p99 traces co-occur with multiple short-lived batch handoffs: the async-batcher exhibits short stall events when bursty traffic and long sequence tokens coincide.
   - Kernel metrics show repeated kernel reinitialization events for the attention path in the same container during these traces (see kernel selection logs). Hypothesis: inefficient kernel warm/cold toggles when sequence length exceeds a threshold and triggers a different kernel path.

3) Network egress and downstream client stalls:
   - ~30% of long p99 traces spent >100ms in network-egress; tcp retransmit counters slightly elevated in a few samples. Not dominant but non-zero.

4) Sequence-length correlated queuing:
   - Observed that long sequences frequently arrive grouped (user behavior: long system messages + followups), creating multi-request batches where the async-batcher increases its wait window to aggregate tokens. This increases p95/p99 but keeps p50 relatively stable.

Replay experiments performed:
- Replayed 120 sample p99 traces under three configs: (A) cache cold, (B) cache forced-warm, (C) batcher aggressive-flush (smaller max-wait). Findings:
  - (A) reproduces KV-read spike + attention stalls (p99 ~1.9s)
  - (B) removes KV-read spike and reduces p99 to ~1.3s
  - (C) reduces p99 to ~850ms but increases CPU utilization and reduces throughput by ~8% in microbench.

Immediate actionable hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: recent cache eviction policy change increased cold-miss rate for specific prompt prefixes. Action: revert the eviction tweak and monitor p99 for 24h (minimal risk).
- H2: kernel selection path flips for >512 token sequences cause reinit stalls at the kernel level. Action: add a guard to avoid kernel reinit in mid-seq handoffs or pre-select path earlier in pipeline. Requires infra/serving runtime change (medium risk).
- H3: batcher wait-time heuristics are tuned too aggressively for bursty long-seq traffic. Action: conservative tweak to flush threshold for endpoints with >10% long-seq traffic (low risk, needs perf regression checks).

Notes / open questions:
- What percentage of affected customers are on Dedicated vs Hosted? Dedicated instances show lower KV-miss variance (probably due to dedicated memory footprint) — need to confirm with product.
- Are there observable correlations with model-quantization profile? A few traces were from models using 8-bit quant, which showed slightly higher decode-loop time.
- Are client SDKs batching requests in a way that causes grouped arrival? Follow up with SDK team.

Proposed near-term playbook items (48-72h):
1) Rollback eviction policy change (owner: Priya) and watch p99 -> immediate observability dashboard to track 1-hour windows.
2) Deploy batcher small-config tweak behind a feature-flag for the endpoint experiencing the worst traffic (owner: Jules).
3) Add higher-fidelity trace tags for kernel selection path and KV cache origin in trace-span (owner: Samir) to make repros easier.
4) Document a reproduction checklist in the Serve Latency Playbook (link in linked_artifacts).

Longer-term work (quarter):
- Kernel warm-path optimization: reduce reinit cost and add pre-selection heuristics (requires GPU infra + runtime engineering).
- KV-cache hit amplification: explore async prefetch of likely prefixes for system-heavy prompts.
- Batcher policy: develop adaptive wait-time based on observed incoming sequence-length histogram per route.

Appendix: exemplar trace notes (anonymized timestamps)
- trace-id: xxxxx-111: timeline shows KV-read at 0.28s, attention stall 0.6-1.4s, emit jitter 1.5-1.65s -> total 1.67s. Notes: cache fallback to slow path.
- trace-id: xxxxx-222: timeline shows no KV spike, but attention loop has 3 micro-pauses aligning to kernel reinit at 0.32s/0.64s/0.98s -> total 1.05s. Notes: kernel path selection flips mid-seq.

If you pick this up:
- Start with quick rollback of eviction policy and enable replay runbook on a 30-min cadence.
- If p99 does not materially improve after rollback, prioritize kernel-selection tracing (Samir).

Unresolved items to log to ticket JIRA-4531:
- exact cache-key heuristics for system prompt prefixes
- kernel-selection metric definitions to publish
- list of endpoints with long-seq traffic >5%

End of notes.

(Informal scratch: saw odd correlation with a batcher GC event on one host — need host-level logs; also one anomalous trace where network egress = 980ms likely client side.)
